correctness.rationale: The joint event all M_r>k_r is exactly the event that each eligible part <=k_r occurs at least once. Deleting one forced copy gives a bijection to partitions of n-T, hence exact p(n-T)/p(n). For k_r=floor(x_r n^1/4), arithmetic progression sums produce T=sqrt(n)/(2h) sum x_r^2+O(n^1/4). Uniform Hardy-Ramanujan logarithmic partition ratio for T=O(sqrt n) then yields product exp(-pi x_r^2/(2h sqrt6)), proving joint weak convergence and iid limiting variables. Continuous limiting laws have no ties, validating the argmin map and 1/|R| probability, while the exact companion coefficient identities give the 1/3 and 2/3 limits. Independently enumerated ordinary partitions at n=14,21,29 for h=2,3,4 and verified the joint mandatory-part event exactly matches the partition-shift count; finite enumeration is only corroboration.
residual_risks: Fixed modulus only; no finite-n independence or quantified convergence rate.

final_claim: For fixed h>=1, the least missing positive part M_r in each residue class r modulo h of a uniform partition of n has jointly independent Rayleigh limits n^-1/4 M_r, survival exp(-pi x^2/(2h sqrt 6)); for any nonempty fixed residue subset the winning class is asymptotically uniform, and the Andrews-El Bachraoui even-companion numbers satisfy a_e(n)=b_e(n)~p(n)/3, t_e(n)~2p(n)/3.
limitations: The modulus and nonempty residue subset must remain fixed as n grows.
